claims.head: The Jets will hunt a mismatch
claims.call: The Jets’ L1 (Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti) spends at least 49% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canadiens’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Scheifele’s line (Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Canadiens’ second line is Texier, Danault and Bolduc.
claims.nums: At home: 49% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 35% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Scott Arniel likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canadiens’ second line.

chips.tip: Winnipeg’s L1 (Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti) at home: 49% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ second lines. Matchups, Winnipeg home games this season, 5 games, 43 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face second lines about 35% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

notes.text: Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský.

Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Kirby Dach has taken his spot beside Alex Newhook and Juraj Slafkovský.
Mike Matheson returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

WPG.head: Nothing to separate these two
WPG.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. Then again, Montréal will be without Suzuki, and Winnipeg has home-ice advantage. For the Jets, the difference could be a penalty kill that holds up.

MTL.head: A genuine toss-up
MTL.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. Then again, Montréal will be without Suzuki, and Winnipeg has home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: The Jets need a win
paras: The Jets are winless in four (0-2-2). The Canadiens are 5-3-2.
At home, Scott Arniel likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canadiens’ second line. The Habs shoot a lot, and the Jets give up plenty.
